metric_defs.name: Composite score
metric_defs.means: Primary ranking metric. Blend of LLM-judge (generative quality) and token F1 / exact-match style extractive overlap. Use this to pick a default method unless your product is judge-only or F1-only.

metric_defs.name: LLM judge
metric_defs.means: A local judge model scores whether the answer is correct / useful relative to gold. Rewards fluent, correct answers even when wording differs from gold. Can be generous to chatty graph answers.

metric_defs.name: Token F1
metric_defs.means: Token overlap between prediction and gold (classic Hotpot-style). Strict: paraphrases score lower. Good for short factual answers.

metric_defs.name: Contains answer
metric_defs.means: Fraction of questions where gold (or key gold tokens / code body) appears in the prediction. Loose recall-style check.

metric_defs.name: Tokens / query
metric_defs.means: Average prompt+completion tokens per question. Proxy for $ and latency. A method with slightly lower quality but far fewer tokens may still be the right production choice.

metric_defs.name: Query latency
metric_defs.means: Mean wall-clock time per question after the index exists.

metric_defs.name: Dual scoreboard / flips
metric_defs.means: Generative winner (judge-heavy) vs composite winner. A flip means the metric you optimize changes who wins — do not trust a single leaderboard number without checking this.

method_defs.Semantic: Dense vector retrieval (embeddings) + LLM generate over top-k chunks.
method_defs.Rerank: Semantic retrieve, then cross-encoder / LLM rerank before generate.
method_defs.BM25+dense: Hybrid sparse (BM25) + dense retrieval fused before generate.
method_defs.Hybrid: Graph + vector hybrid path used in this harness.
method_defs.GraphRAG fast/basic: Microsoft GraphRAG-style fast NLP index + basic/local search (not global).
method_defs.GraphRAG global: Community-summary / global GraphRAG search over the knowledge graph.
method_defs.Frontier: Adaptive routing + corrective RAG style frontier stack.
method_defs.Adaptive: Query router that picks retrieval strategy per question.

benches.title: HotpotQA distractor
benches.what: Multi-hop Wikipedia QA (distractor setting). Each question needs evidence from ≥2 paragraphs; the corpus also includes distractor paragraphs that look related but are not gold.
benches.how_to_read: Higher composite is better. Tokens/query is cost. Graph methods often win on LLM-judge but lose on extractive F1 — check Dual scoreboard and the Quality vs Tokens chart.

meta.note: Full distractor validation = 7405 hard Q / ~66k paragraphs. Local GraphRAG runs are practical at n≈100–500; use n=all only with vector-only methods or a large compute budget.

clear_wins.question: What science fantasy young adult series, told in first person, has a set of companion books narrating the stories of enslaved worlds and alien species?
Who was known by his stage name Aladin and helped organizations improve their performance as a consultant?
The arena where the Lewiston Maineiacs played their home games can seat how many people?
Were Scott Derrickson and Ed Wood of the same nationality?

benches.title: CodeRAG-Bench
benches.what: Code generation with retrieval (Wang et al., NAACL Findings 2025). HumanEval / MBPP / DS-1000 / ODEX. Canonical solutions are leave-gold-out of the datastore.
benches.how_to_read: Code-aware metrics: contains/judge look for function bodies and key tokens, not wiki-style short answers. Prefer composite + judge together.

meta.protocol: Canonical solutions for evaluated tasks are excluded from the retrieval corpus (CodeRAG-Bench leave-gold-out).
meta.note: Full CodeRAG-Bench also includes DS-1000, ODEX, RepoEval, SWE-bench-Lite, and CodeSearchNet-Py. This harness ships the complete basic-programming category (HumanEval 164 + MBPP 500) with the programming-solutions datastore.

benches.title: GraphRAG-Bench Novel
benches.what: Questions designed to test when graph structure helps (Novel-4128 Pepys diary corpus).
benches.how_to_read: If GraphRAG beats semantic here but not on Hotpot, the win is task-specific — do not generalize without checking Hotpot.

findings.obs1: Basic RAG matches GraphRAG on Fact Retrieval
findings.obs2: GraphRAG excels on Complex Reasoning / Summarize / Creative

benches.title: MultiHop-RAG
benches.what: News multi-document reasoning; answers often need several articles.
benches.how_to_read: Compare bridge-style multi-doc questions vs single-hop filters.

meta.note: Closed-world: gold evidence articles + distractors. Use generative_score (judge+contains) for multi-hop fairness.
